transaction_lot_allocations_count.explanation: The 199,998 figure originated from an early generator iteration that assumed 1-to-1 redemption-to-lot allocation (98,994 redemptions + 20,000 reversals + 80,996 expiries + 8 anomaly duplicates = 199,998), which caused lot balance overdraws. The corrected FIFO accounting engine strictly respects lot remaining balances; 1,088 redemptions split across two open lots, resulting in 100,082 redemption allocations, 81,004 expiry allocations, and 20,000 reversal allocations = 201,086 rows. This matches data/loyalty_ledger.db, dataset_manifest.json, and all CSV/JSON export files.

redemptions_with_0_allocations.explanation: These are the two intentionally injected AN-002 over-redemption anomaly cases. Because the account possessed zero points, the redemptions were erroneously approved without lot backing and therefore generated zero lot allocation records.

redemption_allocation_arithmetic_reconci.apparent_two_row_discrepancy_explanation: An auditor calculating 98,996 + 1,088 = 100,084 assumes all 98,996 redemptions have at least one allocation. In reality, exactly 98,994 baseline redemptions have allocations (98,994 + 1,088 = 100,082), while the 2 AN-002 anomaly redemptions intentionally have 0 allocations.

EXPIRY.formula: 80988 (single-expiry lots) + 16 (8 lots with 2 AN-004 duplicate expiries) = 81004

REVERSAL.formula: 20000 baseline returns with linked reversals = 20000 (2 AN-003 returns have NULL reversals)

an_001_canonical_definition.definition: Stored account balance differs from ledger sum (account.cached_balance_points != sum(tx.points_delta))
an_001_canonical_definition.alignment: Consistent across PRD.md, business_rules.md, data_dictionary.md, anomaly_injector.py, detector.py, ground_truth.json, and evaluation_metrics.json.

AN-001.scenario: Stored balance differs from ledger sum

AN-003.scenario: Returned order keeps all earned points (missing reversal)

AN-005.scenario: Tier uses gross rather than qualifying spend
